title: All 32 NHL Logos Ranked
author: Arek Dvornechuck

seo.title: All 32 NHL Logos Ranked
seo.description: Every NHL team logo ranked from best to worst, with a designer's breakdown of all 32 crests, from the Rangers and Red Wings to the new Utah Mammoth.

description: Every NHL team logo ranked from best to worst, with a designer's breakdown of all 32 crests, from the Rangers and Red Wings to the new Utah Mammoth.
body:
Introduction

Today, I'm going to the New York Rangers vs. Vegas Golden Knights game and as a logo designer—I couldn't help but analyzed the logo designs of NHL teams.

Great logos tell a story: they capture local culture, team history, and the spirit of the sport in just a few shapes and colors.

With that in mind, I’ve ranked all 32 NHL team logos for the 2026–27 season, from my favorite to my least favorite—including the newest one in the league, the Utah Mammoth.

Hockey logos are some of the most distinctive in sports. Many of them are full illustrations, like the Florida Panthers or the Chicago Blackhawks, while others rely on a single, bold letterform, like the Seattle Kraken.

Here are a few of the standouts at a glance, before we go through every team one by one.

All 32 NHL Logos, Ranked:

  1. New York Rangers
  2. Vegas Golden Knights
  3. Florida Panthers
  4. Nashville Predators
  5. Dallas Stars
  6. Tampa Bay Lightning
  7. Pittsburgh Penguins
  8. Philadelphia Flyers
  9. Chicago Blackhawks
  10. Seattle Kraken
  11. Toronto Maple Leafs
  12. Detroit Red Wings
  13. Montreal Canadiens
  14. Boston Bruins
  15. St. Louis Blues
  16. Minnesota Wild
  17. Vancouver Canucks
  18. Winnipeg Jets
  19. Utah Mammoth
  20. Edmonton Oilers
  21. New Jersey Devils
  22. Carolina Hurricanes
  23. Anaheim Ducks
  24. Washington Capitals
  25. Calgary Flames
  26. Ottawa Senators
  27. San Jose Sharks
  28. Colorado Avalanche
  29. Buffalo Sabres
  30. Los Angeles Kings
  31. New York Islanders
  32. Columbus Blue Jackets

Plus a bonus pick: the Hartford Whalers.

I've broken them down by design elements together with my personal opinion on what makes each one stand out.

1. New York Rangers

Founded in 1926, the New York Rangers quickly became one of the NHL’s “Original Six” franchises.

Their success in 1928 made them the first American team to win the Stanley Cup, planting hockey’s roots firmly in New York City.

Over the decades, they’ve built fierce rivalries with neighbors like the Islanders and Devils, and continue to be an iconic presence at Madison Square Garden.

Design Breakdown

  • Classic shield design with 2 distinct notches.
  • Powerful, American red, blue and white color palette.
  • The name “RANGERS” set at 45 degree angle.

My Opinion

  • Timeless and distinct shape and color palette.
  • Minimalist, clean logo makes it look good on merchandise.
  • Diagonal text look iconic on jerseys.

2. Vegas Golden Knights

The Vegas Golden Knights are one of the NHL’s newest teams, joining the league in the 2017–18 season.

They shocked fans and pundits alike by reaching the Stanley Cup Final in their inaugural year.

Named to reflect Nevada’s historical ties to precious metals and the valor of medieval knights, they’ve quickly developed a loyal and passionate fan base.

Design Breakdown

  • A stylized knight’s helmet in regal gold, silver and black.
  • A subtle “V” for Vegas in the negative space.
  • Shield symbol stands for protection/authority.

My Opinion

  • Clean, bold and instantly recognizable logo.
  • The gold accent pops against the black.
  • Cleverly hidden "V" letter in negative space.

3. Florida Panthers

Established in 1993, the Florida Panthers were part of the NHL’s push to expand hockey’s footprint in the Sunshine State—Florida.

Their name honors the endangered Florida panther, native to the region.

They made an early splash by reaching the Stanley Cup Final in 1996, endearing themselves to the local sports scene.

Design Breakdown

  • A shield-style crest featuring a panther head in profile.
  • Color palette: navy, gold, red create military-like aesthetic.
  • Prominently displayed name on red background.

My Opinion

  • The modern design style make it look contemporary.
  • Still uniquely Floridian, but with a mature, refined style.
  • Great use of negative space and well-balanced colors.

4. Nashville Predators

The Nashville Predators joined the NHL as an expansion team in 1998, bringing top-tier hockey to Tennessee.

Their name and mascot were inspired by a prehistoric saber-toothed cat fossil found under a Nashville building site.

Over the years, they’ve cultivated a passionate fan base famous for country music–themed traditions.

Design Breakdown

  • A saber-tooth cat’s head in profile (predator).
  • Dynamic motion adds to cat’s fierce expression.
  • Unique color palette and sharp, aggressive lines.

My Opinion

  • Captures the team’s aggressive, high-energy style.
  • The angular look feels modern yet ties to ancient fossil origins.
  • Bright yellow/gold contrast well with dark navy blue.

5. Dallas Stars

Originally the Minnesota North Stars (1967), the franchise relocated to Dallas in 1993, dropping the “North” from their name.

They achieved a major milestone by winning the Stanley Cup in 1999, solidifying hockey’s presence in Texas.

The team’s identity continues to blend Lone Star State pride with a modern aesthetic.

Design Breakdown

  • A silver “D” for Dallas forming a star shape around it.
  • Unique color palette: victory green, silver and black.
  • The “D-star” is sleek, modern, and easy to place on jerseys.

My Opinion

  • The green stands out in the NHL, giving the brand fresh energy.
  • Merging the “D” with a star symbolizes both: team and state.
  • Overall, a clean, polished emblem that looks good on merch.

6. Tampa Bay Lightning

Joining the league in 1992, the Tampa Bay Lightning helped introduce hockey to central Florida.

They’re nicknamed the “Bolts,” tying in with Florida’s reputation for frequent thunderstorms.

The franchise has captured multiple Stanley Cups, solidifying their status as a powerhouse in the modern NHL era.

Design Breakdown

  • A simplified lightning bolt in a circle, set in unicolor.
  • Modern, minimal aesthetic with few extraneous details.
  • Occasionally uses a “BOLTS” wordmark for alternate jerseys.

My Opinion

  • Clean and bold; the lightning bolt is instantly recognizable.
  • Blue-and-white palette is classic yet stands out on the ice.
  • Probably the most minimalist logo, but still as impactful as others.

7. Pittsburgh Penguins

The Pittsburgh Penguins were part of the NHL’s 1967 expansion.

Their name was chosen to tie in with the icy conditions of the Civic Arena, nicknamed “The Igloo.”

A series of star players—Mario Lemieux, Jaromír Jágr, and Sidney Crosby—helped the team secure multiple Stanley Cup wins, endearing them to fans worldwide.

Design Breakdown

  • A cartoon-style penguin with a hockey stick.
  • The gold triangle representing Pittsburgh’s Golden Triangle area.
  • Sharp lines but also playful and iconic.

My Opinion

  • Balances fun character design with a strong sports identity.
  • The color scheme ties perfectly to Pittsburgh’s unified branding.
  • Beloved by fans, especially for its nostalgic tie to classic team eras.

8. Philadelphia Flyers

Joining the NHL in the 1967 expansion, the Philadelphia Flyers quickly made a name for themselves by winning consecutive Stanley Cups in 1974 and 1975.

Known as the “Broad Street Bullies” for their rough-and-tumble play, they have remained a notable force in the Eastern Conference.

Their rabid fan base and storied history make them a quintessential Philly team.

Design Breakdown

  • The winged “P” with an orange circle “eye.”
  • Distinct color scheme black, orange, and white.
  • Unchanged since its inception, a testament to its strong initial design.

My Opinion

  • One of the most recognizable letter-based logos in sports.
  • The P feels gritty, reflecting Philly’s tough reputation.
  • A great example of how a single letter can form a great logo.

9. Chicago Blackhawks

As one of the NHL’s Original Six teams, the Chicago Blackhawks date back to 1926.

They were named after the “Blackhawk Division” of the owner’s Army Infantry Division.

They have won multiple Stanley Cups and are considered one of the league’s most storied franchises.

Design Breakdown

  • A Native American "Blackhawsk" head in profile.
  • Pretty detailed design in comparison to many sports logos.
  • Has become synonymous with tradition and legacy.

My Opinion

  • Visually striking and instantly recognizable (although could be simplified).
  • From a purely aesthetic standpoint, it’s one of the most artistic logos in the NHL.
  • Continues to spark cultural conversations about representation, reflecting evolving social awareness.

10. Seattle Kraken

The Seattle Kraken joined the NHL for the 2021–22 season, introducing top-tier hockey to the Pacific Northwest.

Their name references the mythical sea creature, nodding to the region’s maritime culture and folklore.

Despite being new to the league, they’ve quickly cultivated a dedicated following with their unique brand.

Design Breakdown

  • A stylized “S” for Seattle with a red eye.
  • Color palette: deep sea blue, ice blue, and red accents for contrast.
  • A subtle tentacle referencing Seattle’s nautical history.

My Opinion

  • Cleverly blending a single letter with a subtle creature element.
  • The layered blues evoke the depths of the ocean, setting the mood.
  • Already considered one of the best contemporary NHL logos.

11. Toronto Maple Leafs

Founded in 1917, the Toronto Maple Leafs are an Original Six franchise and a cornerstone of Canadian hockey.

The name pays tribute to Canada’s national symbol, the maple leaf, emphasizing national pride.

Despite a long championship drought, the team’s fervent fan base remains one of the largest in the league.

Design Breakdown

  • A stylized maple leaf in navy blue and white.
  • Features sharper edges and vein details.
  • The single-color logo looks good on merch.

My Opinion

  • Patriotic and instantly linked to hockey tradition.
  • Evolved without straying from its iconic roots.
  • A prime example of a logo that seamlessly blends national pride and local fandom.

12. Detroit Red Wings

The Detroit Red Wings date back to 1926 and took their current name in 1932, when owner James Norris brought over the winged wheel from his old Montreal club.

It's an Original Six team with 11 Stanley Cups, and the logo has barely changed in over 90 years.

Design Breakdown

  • A spoked car wheel with a single wing sweeping back from it.
  • The wheel is a direct nod to Detroit as the Motor City.
  • Drawn in one flat red on white, with no gradients or outlines.

My Opinion

  • One of the best examples of a logo that tells you where the team is from.
  • The wing gives a static wheel a real sense of speed.
  • It works in one color, at any size, which is why it has never needed a redesign.

13. Montreal Canadiens

Founded in 1909, the Montreal Canadiens are the oldest team in professional hockey and the most successful, with 24 Stanley Cups.

Their famous “CH” stands for Club de Hockey Canadien. The popular story that the H means “Habitants” is a myth, even though the nickname “Habs” stuck.

Design Breakdown

  • A red “C” wrapped around a white “H”, forming one compact monogram.
  • A thin blue outline completes the red, white, and blue palette.
  • Heavy, rounded letterforms that read clearly from the top row of the arena.

My Opinion

  • A perfect monogram: two letters, one shape, zero clutter.
  • It feels historic without looking dated.
  • Like the Yankees “NY”, it has become bigger than the sport itself.

14. Boston Bruins

The Boston Bruins joined the NHL in 1924 as the league's first American team and celebrated their 100th season in 2023–24.

The spoked “B” has been their main mark since 1948, and its spokes are often read as a nod to Boston's nickname, “The Hub”.

Design Breakdown

  • A bold black “B” set inside a wheel with six spokes.
  • A strict two-color palette of black and gold.
  • A thick outer ring that turns the letter into a badge.

My Opinion

  • Simple, tough, and instantly recognizable on a jersey or a hat.
  • The black and gold combination is one of the strongest in sports.
  • Proof that a single letter can carry a century of history.

15. St. Louis Blues

The St. Louis Blues joined the NHL in the 1967 expansion and won their first Stanley Cup in 2019.

The team is named after W.C. Handy's song “St. Louis Blues”, so the logo is a blue note with a wing.

Design Breakdown

  • A musical note whose flag turns into a wing.
  • Two shades of blue with a touch of yellow.
  • No letters at all: the name is told through a symbol.

My Opinion

  • One of the cleverest names-to-symbol translations in sports.
  • The clean silhouette holds up at tiny sizes.
  • It ties the team to the city's music culture without being literal.

16. Minnesota Wild

The Minnesota Wild entered the NHL in 2000, bringing the league back to the State of Hockey after the North Stars left for Dallas.

Their logo is famous for showing two pictures at once.

Design Breakdown

  • The outline of a wild animal's head, facing left.
  • Inside it, a Minnesota landscape: pine trees, a river, a sunset sky, and a shooting star.
  • The star nods to Minnesota's motto, “L'Étoile du Nord”, and the departed North Stars.

My Opinion

  • A smart use of figure and ground: you see the animal, then the scenery.
  • It packs a lot of detail, so it's weaker at small sizes.
  • Still one of the most original concepts in the league.

17. Vancouver Canucks

The Vancouver Canucks joined the NHL in 1970, and their logo history includes some of the league's wildest designs.

Since 2007, the primary logo has been the orca, first introduced in 1997.

Design Breakdown

  • An orca whale bursting out of the ice, its body curving into a “C”.
  • Styling inspired by the Indigenous art of the Pacific Northwest.
  • Navy, blue, and green that reflect the coast.

My Opinion

  • The letter and the animal are one idea, which is hard to pull off.
  • It feels rooted in place, not just in sport.
  • Calmer than the famous 1978 “flying V”, and much better for it.

18. Winnipeg Jets

The current Winnipeg Jets arrived in 2011, when the Atlanta Thrashers relocated to Manitoba.

The logo pays tribute to the Royal Canadian Air Force, which has deep roots in Winnipeg.

Design Breakdown

  • A circular roundel borrowed from military aircraft markings.
  • A silver fighter jet pointing straight up over a red maple leaf.
  • Navy, aviation blue, silver, and red.

My Opinion

  • Disciplined and symmetrical, it feels like an official insignia.
  • The military reference gives the name real meaning.
  • Maybe a little too serious for some fans, but it's very well crafted.

19. Utah Mammoth

Utah's NHL team started play in 2024 after the Arizona Coyotes' hockey operations moved to Salt Lake City.

After one season as the Utah Hockey Club, the team became the Utah Mammoth in May 2025, with a new “Mountain Mammoth” logo.

Design Breakdown

  • A charging mammoth head with its tusk curving up into a “U”.
  • Snow-capped Wasatch Mountains form the top of its head, and the ear hides the outline of Utah.
  • Colors named Rock Black, Mountain Blue, and Salt White.

My Opinion

  • The newest logo in the league and already one of the most talked-about.
  • Lots of hidden details, but the silhouette stays bold.
  • A good lesson in how much local storytelling you can fit into one mark.

20. Edmonton Oilers

The Edmonton Oilers started in the WHA in 1972 and joined the NHL in 1979.

Led by Wayne Gretzky, they won five Stanley Cups between 1984 and 1990.

Design Breakdown

  • A blue circle with the word “OILERS” set in heavy capitals.
  • An orange oil drop sits above the name, a nod to Alberta's oil industry.
  • A classic blue and orange palette.

My Opinion

  • Not flashy, but clear and honest about where the team comes from.
  • The drop is a tiny detail that does a lot of work.
  • Feels like a retro sports badge in the best way.

21. New Jersey Devils

The franchise began as the Kansas City Scouts in 1974, moved to Colorado, and settled in New Jersey in 1982.

The name comes from the Jersey Devil, a creature from New Jersey folklore.

Design Breakdown

  • An “N” and “J” joined into one monogram.
  • The J grows horns at the top and a pointed tail at the bottom.
  • Red and black, set inside a white circle.

My Opinion

  • A fun, clever monogram that adds personality without a mascot drawing.
  • The letters are a little hard to read at first glance.
  • Still, it's unmistakably the Devils.

22. Carolina Hurricanes

The Carolina Hurricanes moved to Raleigh in 1997. Before that, they were the Hartford Whalers (see the bonus pick below).

They won the Stanley Cup in 2006.

Design Breakdown

  • A red and black hurricane swirl, like a storm seen on a weather map.
  • A black puck sits in the eye of the storm.
  • Colors inspired by the red and black hurricane warning flags.

My Opinion

  • Strong sense of motion for a static logo.
  • The puck in the eye is a smart, simple detail.
  • It looks a bit 90s, but it still works.

23. Anaheim Ducks

The team was founded in 1993 by Disney as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, named after the hit movie.

In 2024, the Ducks went orange and brought back an updated version of the original duck-mask logo.

Design Breakdown

  • A duck's head wearing a goalie mask, framed by crossed sticks.
  • A triangle shape behind it, from the original Mighty Ducks logo.
  • New orange, black, and gold colors, a nod to Orange County.

My Opinion

  • A great example of nostalgia done right.
  • Much more characterful than the webbed-foot “D” it replaced.
  • The orange makes the team stand out in a league full of navy.

24. Washington Capitals

The Washington Capitals joined the NHL in 1974 and won their first Stanley Cup in 2018.

In 2007, the team returned to a modern version of its original wordmark logo.

Design Breakdown

  • The word “capitals” in lowercase italic letters.
  • The “t” is drawn as a hockey stick.
  • Three stars above, inspired by the District of Columbia flag.

My Opinion

  • A wordmark is a bold choice in a league full of crests.
  • The stick and stars feel patriotic without being heavy-handed.
  • It reads a little small on a jersey compared to a big symbol.

25. Calgary Flames

The Flames started in Atlanta in 1972 and moved to Calgary in 1980.

They kept the name, and the flame idea carried over into the logo.

Design Breakdown

  • A bold red “C” with flames trailing off the back.
  • Yellow and gold flames, outlined in black.
  • Italic angle that suggests forward motion.

My Opinion

  • Direct and easy to read, even from far away.
  • Very literal, but sports fans like literal.
  • A good letter-based logo that owns its color.

26. Ottawa Senators

The modern Ottawa Senators joined the NHL in 1992, reviving the name of an early Ottawa club that won many Stanley Cups.

In 2020, they returned to a flat “2D” version of their original centurion logo.

Design Breakdown

  • The profile of a Roman senator wearing a gold helmet with a red crest.
  • A flowing cape set inside a black circle.
  • Red, black, and gold.

My Opinion

  • A stronger, flatter look than the 3D version they dropped.
  • The Roman theme connects to the name, though not to the city.
  • Detailed, but well balanced.

27. San Jose Sharks

The San Jose Sharks joined the NHL in 1991, bringing the league back to the Bay Area.

Their teal was a bold choice at the time and quickly made their merchandise a hit.

Design Breakdown

  • A shark bursting through a triangle, biting a hockey stick.
  • Teal, black, white, and a touch of orange.
  • Sharp angles that suggest speed and aggression.

My Opinion

  • Very 90s, in a fun way.
  • The stick in the mouth says “hockey” without any lettering.
  • Busier than it needs to be, but memorable.

28. Colorado Avalanche

The Colorado Avalanche moved from Quebec, where they were the Nordiques, in 1995.

They won the Stanley Cup in their very first season in Denver, and again in 2001 and 2022.

Design Breakdown

  • A burgundy “A” shaped like a mountain peak.
  • A blue and white swoosh of snow wraps around it.
  • A puck sits at the bottom of the swoosh.

My Opinion

  • A nice link between the name and the Rocky Mountains.
  • The swoosh adds energy but also visual noise.
  • Feels dated next to newer, flatter logos.

29. Buffalo Sabres

The Buffalo Sabres joined the NHL in 1970.

After trying several designs, they returned to their classic royal blue and gold logo in 2020.

Design Breakdown

  • A buffalo leaping over two crossed sabres.
  • Set inside a blue circle with a gold outline.
  • A simple, badge-like layout.

My Opinion

  • Going back to the original was the right call.
  • Clear symbols, but the buffalo is a bit small and thin.
  • A charming vintage logo.

30. Los Angeles Kings

The Los Angeles Kings joined the NHL in the 1967 expansion and won Stanley Cups in 2012 and 2014.

In 2024, they introduced a new primary logo built around a chevron-shaped shield.

Design Breakdown

  • The word “KINGS” in bold italic letters inside a shield.
  • A small crown at the bottom and “Los Angeles” at the top.
  • Silver, black, and white.

My Opinion

  • The silver and black still carry the Gretzky-era energy.
  • The shield shape feels a bit generic.
  • Clean and professional, but not very distinctive.

31. New York Islanders

The New York Islanders joined the NHL in 1972 and won four straight Stanley Cups from 1980 to 1983.

Their logo has stayed close to the original for more than 50 years.

Design Breakdown

  • A blue circle with a bold orange “NY”.
  • A map of Long Island runs across the middle.
  • A hockey stick forms the leg of the Y, with “ISLANDERS” below.

My Opinion

  • The map is a nice, local detail.
  • Lots of elements fighting for attention.
  • Loved by fans for its history more than its design.

32. Columbus Blue Jackets

The Columbus Blue Jackets joined the NHL in 2000.

The name honors Ohio's role in the Civil War, when many Ohio soldiers wore blue Union jackets.

Design Breakdown

  • A red, white, and blue ribbon forming a “C”, inspired by the Ohio state flag.
  • A silver star in the center.
  • Navy blue background.

My Opinion

  • The story behind it is strong.
  • The mark itself looks generic, like many other patriotic logos.
  • Hard to remember compared to the rest of the league.

Bonus: Hartford Whalers

The Whalers franchise began in the World Hockey Association (WHA) as the New England Whalers in 1972.

Note that this is a Historic/Defunct team, which now became the Carolina Hurricanes, but the logo is so iconic—so I decided to describe it.

When the WHA merged with the NHL, the team moved to Hartford and became the Hartford Whalers.

Although they relocated in 1997 (becoming the Carolina Hurricanes), the Whalers’ brand endures as a nostalgic fan favorite.‍

Design Breakdown

  • A whale tail on top and an “H” hidden and "W" below.
  • Colors: green, blue, and white—fresh and maritime-themed.
  • Often celebrated as one of hockey’s best “hidden message” logos.

My Opinion

  • Iconic for its excellent use of the negative-space.
  • The playful color palette stands out among other NHL logos.
  • Lives on in throwback merch, proving great design can outlast a franchise’s actual run.

Conclusion

Hockey logos blend team identity with local culture and a dash of creative flair.

From the timeless, shield-based design of the New York Rangers to the imaginative letter-art of the Seattle Kraken, each of the 32 crests reflects a franchise’s unique heritage and aspirations.

Even historical gems like the Hartford Whalers continue to captivate design enthusiasts and fans decades after relocation.

But let’s not forget the NHL Shield itself—a monochrome emblem featuring a shield outline and diagonal lettering.

Originally introduced in 1917, it’s undergone a few updates, with the most recent version leaning into a sleek black-and-silver color scheme.

The league’s logo embodies the overarching spirit of hockey, providing a clean, authoritative backdrop for all these team identities we’ve explored.

It’s a fitting symbol for a sport whose branding can be as intense and dynamic as the action on the ice.
